subject: PulseHealth: DPA redlines, SOC2 evidence & eSign routing
body:
From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo earlier — we loved the latency numbers. Legal at PulseHealth asked me to circulate our DPA review and a short list of evidence items they need before procurement completes the PO. High level asks:
- Can you confirm you will sign our standard DPA with the three redlines attached (retention carveout, EU SCCs clause insertion, and HIPAA BAA language)?
- Can you provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report or SOC 2 summary and a CAIQ/consensus answers doc?
- We need the signature path and expected timeline — will an exec at Redwood sign or does legal need to route to sales?

I've attached our redlined DPA (PulseHealth_DPA_redline_v2.docx) to this message. We would like to close this before the end of next week if possible.

Best,
Emma Rodriguez
Senior Counsel, PulseHealth

----- Original message attached -----

From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com>
Sent: Friday, June 14, 2028 9:12 AM
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Subject: PulseHealth DPA redlines (attached)


---
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Emma — thanks for the note and for sharing the redlines. Looping in Neha (privacy counsel) and Irene (legal ops) to confirm scope and evidence items.

Neha / Irene — per PulseHealth's redline we have three notable asks: 1) retention carveout (they want shorter retention for analytics logs), 2) SCCs insertion for EU subprocessor transfers, and 3) an optional BAA/HIPAA clause. PulseHealth is asking for our SOC 2 Type II summary and a CAIQ-equivalent.

Can you advise:
- Whether we can accept a limited retention carveout (suggested reply: accept with a 30/90 day compromise and explicit purpose limitation)?
- If SCC insertion requires a separate addendum or we can reference our standard SCC mapping?
- Do we need to sign a BAA or can we provide the HIPAA controls summary and confirm contractual commitments?

I'll prepare a consolidated redline and propose an eSign route (legal -> exec signoff -> PulseHealth). If legal prefers a different routing (e.g., sales-level sign for standard customers), please flag.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_clean_v1.docx (for reference)

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----- On Fri, Jun 14, 2028 at 11:18 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote: -----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Thanks Mateo — quick take from privacy:

1) Retention carveout: we can be flexible on analytics logs but need a strict purpose and a maximum retention window. Recommend counter-proposing 90 days for analytics logs and 30 days for request-level debug logs.

2) SCCs: insertion is OK but we should add an internal mapping reference to our vendor subprocessor list and confirm that the SCCs apply to transfers we initiate (we control some subprocessor relationships). We prefer referencing our "SCCs Annex" rather than modifying the master text; that keeps consistency across contracts.

3) HIPAA / BAA: PulseHealth is a covered entity — we should not sign their full BAA as-is. Provide the HIPAA controls summary and offer a narrow BAA limited to PHI processing activities identified in the SOW. If Pulse insists on full BAA language, escalate to exec legal.

Evidence list to share (we can provide redacted items):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) or a one-page SOC 2 summary (controls mapped)
- CAIQ / consensus answers for cloud security questions
- Subprocessor list and data residency notes
- DPIA summary if they request EU processing details

I'll attach a redacted SOC2 summary now (redacted_SOC2_summary.pdf). Marcus — can you confirm if procurement should accept an exec signature for this deal (deal size looks like $120k ARR commit)? Also flag any billing/commitment exceptions we need to coordinate.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

----- On Fri, Jun 14, 2028 at 13:07 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote: -----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Thanks Neha — procurement/partnerships perspective:

- Deal size and strategic value: PulseHealth is in the target vertical (healthcare) so we should be willing to accept a narrow BAA and the SCC annex. Exec signoff (VP/COO level) is preferred for any contract including HIPAA carveouts.
- eSign path: legal ops to prepare DocuSign envelope -> send to VP Legal for final signature -> execute. Irene, can your team prepare the DocuSign and set an internal approver?
- Retention: agree with Neha's counters (90/30). Let's avoid making product changes; keep the carveout contractual only.

One ask — confirm whether the subprocessor list includes our EU inference cluster provider (they need to be referenced explicitly for SCC mapping). If not present, Irene please add the infra provider and the region mapping.

Marcus Lin
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

----- On Mon, Jun 16, 2028 at 09:32 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote: -----
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com>, PulseHealth Legal <legal@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Hi all — legal ops has prepared the consolidated redline (attached) and the DocuSign envelope. Summary of changes we pushed to PulseHealth redline:
- Accepted retention compromise: analytics logs 90 days, debug requests 30 days; added purpose limitation and deletion flow.
- Referred to Redwood "SCCs Annex" (not inline insertion) and provided mapping to our infra providers (including EU inference cluster: eu-infer-1).
- Offered a narrow BAA limited to the SOW — asked PulseHealth to confirm whether they'll provide a SOW that enumerates PHI categories.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-pulse-dpa (live for countersign)
Attachments: PulseHealth_DPA_redline_v2.docx (counter-proposed)

Emma — when you're ready we can route to VP Legal (Marcus) for signature. Expected internal SLA: 24 hours to obtain exec sign-off after PulseHealth acknowledges the counter.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Legal Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

----- On Mon, Jun 16, 2028 at 15:47 Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com> wrote: -----
From: Emma Rodriguez <emma@pulsehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, PulseHealth Legal <legal@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines / SOC2 / eSign path

Irene / Mateo — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the counter-proposal and the edits look acceptable. PulseHealth will sign the DocuSign envelope; our GC will countersign.

Two quick asks before final execution: can you confirm the SOC2 redacted summary covers the last audit window (Apr 2027 - Mar 2028)? Also, please confirm that the SCCs Annex references the eu-infer-1 cluster.

If those are confirmed, we'll complete signature today. Appreciate everyone's responsiveness.

Best,
Emma Rodriguez
Senior Counsel, PulseHealth

[Attachment stubs: PulseHealth_DPA_redline_v2.docx (redline); redacted_SOC2_summary.pdf (redacted)]
